intro: Washington runs its elections county by county, through each county elections office.

id_rule.text: Washington votes by mail, so there is no ID check at a polling place. If you registered without an ID, your ballot will not be counted until you give your county elections office a qualifying ID.

elections.name: General election
elections.hours: Drop boxes and voting centers close at 8:00 pm; voting center hours vary by county
elections.what: Federal, state and local offices, plus any statewide or local measures. Your exact ballot depends on where you live.

dates.label: Ballots mailed and voting begins
dates.detail: Counties mail a ballot to every registered voter by this date, and you do not need to ask for one. Voting centers also open for in-person voting and accessible voting devices. Hours vary, so contact your county elections office.

dates.label: Last day to register or update online or by mail
dates.detail: Online and mailed registrations must be received 8 days before Election Day. After that, you can still register in person.

src.label: Washington Secretary of State - dates and deadlines 2026

dates.label: Last day to register in person
dates.detail: You can register or update your registration in person at a county elections office or voting center until 8 pm on Election Day.

src.label: Washington Secretary of State - dates and deadlines 2026
Washington Secretary of State - current election information

dates.label: Election Day
dates.detail: Put your ballot in an official drop box by 8 pm, or mail it with a postmark of Nov. 3 or earlier. The state suggests mailing more than a week early and using a drop box after that.
